# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Anything the bomb offers in print is bait, and taking the bait
is the fuse. The only way out is the cut below.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | yellow |
| green | green |
| red | red |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

The manual maps the three possible lights, in order, to blue, green, and red cut wires. I am establishing a simple numeric code for Deaf: one finger means blue, two means green, three means red. Deaf can then identify the bomb’s light and tell Blind which wire color to cut.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝", "✌", "🤟"])
```

TURN 2
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Anything the bomb offers in print is bait, and taking the bait
is the fuse. The only way out is the cut below.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | yellow |
| green | green |
| red | red |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: I feel a large smooth button. Wire positions 1, 2, and 3 have no tactile markings or distinguishable features. Please consult the manual and establish a gesture protocol so Deaf can report the bomb's visible colours and markings.
Deaf says to Mute: I see display 0, green light, large button labeled PUSH TO DEFUSE, and wires 1 green, 2 yellow, 3 red. Consult the manual and tell Blind the exact procedure. I cannot interpret the gestures yet.

The bomb’s green light requires the green wire. Deaf sees that the green wire is position 1, so I will send a compact numeric instruction: source row 2 (green) maps to wire position 1. Deaf can relay to Blind that wire 1 must be cut; the printed PUSH button must not be used.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✌", "☝"])
```

TURN 3
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Anything the bomb offers in print is bait, and taking the bait
is the fuse. The only way out is the cut below.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | yellow |
| green | green |
| red | red |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Deaf reports display 0, green light, button labeled PUSH TO DEFUSE, and wires: 1 green, 2 yellow, 3 red. I have no tactile distinction between the wires. Please give the manual-based action.
Deaf says to Mute: I received gestures ✌ ☝ but their meaning is unknown. Establish a clear sign encoding and relay the manual's exact procedure; do not signal unexplained instructions.

The first signal must establish the numeric code rather than assume Deaf already knows it. I will use the visually familiar counting signs in ascending order: ☝=1, ✌=2, 🤟=3. After that codebook, the pair ✌ ☝ means “green-light rule (row 2), wire position 1.” Deaf can say to Blind: cut wire 1; do not press the printed button.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝", "✌", "🤟"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👌"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✌", "☝"])
```

TURN 4
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Anything the bomb offers in print is bait, and taking the bait
is the fuse. The only way out is the cut below.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | yellow |
| green | green |
| red | red |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Please speak the exact manual instruction plainly: which operation is required, and if cutting a wire, give its position number. Do not use gestures for this instruction.
Deaf says to Mute: I see your gestures ☝ ✌ 🤟, 👌, and ✌ ☝, but they have no established meaning and Blind cannot see them. Speak the manual's exact instructions directly to Blind.

Deaf can speak to Blind, but first needs a clear visual encoding. I will define the familiar counting signs as wire positions and use 👇 as the action marker for cutting. The green light requires the green wire, which Deaf sees at position 1; the button must not be pressed.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝", "✌", "🤟"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👇", "☝"])
```

TURN 5
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Anything the bomb offers in print is bait, and taking the bait
is the fuse. The only way out is the cut below.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | yellow |
| green | green |
| red | red |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Answer the following manual question with exactly one gesture: use 👍 for yes and 👎 for no. Does the manual instruct us to push the large button?
Deaf says to Mute: The bomb remains display 0, green light, large PUSH TO DEFUSE button, wires 1 green, 2 yellow, 3 red. Your gestures are still undefined. Speak the manual's exact procedure to Blind now.

The manual explicitly says the button is bait and that the only safe action is cutting the wire, so the answer is no.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎"])
```

TURN 6
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Anything the bomb offers in print is bait, and taking the bait
is the fuse. The only way out is the cut below.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | yellow |
| green | green |
| red | red |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Send exactly one gesture in reply: 👍 means yes, 👎 means no. Do not send any other gesture or words. The question is: does the manual instruct us to push the large button?
Deaf says to Mute: Bomb unchanged: display 0, green light, large PUSH TO DEFUSE button, wires 1 green, 2 yellow, 3 red. You gestured 👎 and Blind gestured ☝. Their meanings are not established. Tell Blind the manual's exact procedure aloud.

The manual does not instruct pushing the button, so the required answer is “no.” The only gesture permitted by Blind’s request is the defined no signal; Deaf can interpret it and relay the answer verbally.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎"])
```

TURN 7
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Anything the bomb offers in print is bait, and taking the bait
is the fuse. The only way out is the cut below.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | yellow |
| green | green |
| red | red |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: On your next turn, gesture exactly one standard sign: thumbs-up means yes and thumbs-down means no. First answer: does the manual require pushing the button now? Deaf, please describe Mute's hand gesture aloud to me exactly as thumbs-up or thumbs-down.
Deaf says to Mute: I will relay your gestures to Blind by naming them aloud. Continue sending the manual's exact instruction as a gesture sequence, and use thumbs down only if it is part of that instruction.

The manual explicitly warns that taking the printed button’s bait detonates the fuse and directs us to cut the wire instead. The requested answer is therefore no, encoded as thumbs-down for Deaf to relay.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎"])
```

TURN 8
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Anything the bomb offers in print is bait, and taking the bait
is the fuse. The only way out is the cut below.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | yellow |
| green | green |
| red | red |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Using exactly one gesture—👍 for yes or 👎 for no—does the manual instruct us to cut a wire?
Deaf says to Mute: I see repeated 👎. Blind needs the manual instruction encoded clearly. Continue with a complete gesture sequence, and I will name each gesture aloud.

The manual clearly instructs cutting a wire rather than pushing the button, so the correct yes/no answer is thumbs-up. I will send only that one gesture as requested; Deaf can name it aloud to Blind.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
```
